lines.li: [us] Welcome, I hope the road wasn't hard on you.
[them,their:tribal] We walked from first light, and here we are.
[them,their:empire] It was long, but an invitation is an invitation.
[them] Long enough to be hungry, which I'm told is the right way to arrive.
[us] Then you came to the right place today.
[us] Are you taking part in any of the contests?
[them,their:tribal] I run, and I wrestle, and I lose at neither if I can help it.
[them,their:medieval] I'll try the wrestling, though my reeve says I shouldn't.
[them,their:industrial] I'll race if my knees agree to it.
[them,their:spacer] I came to watch, mostly, and to keep score.
[them] If they'll have me, I'd like to try.
[us] We'll see you at the gate, then.
[us] How do your people keep a feast at home?
[them,their:tribal] A great hunt first, then wrestling and races until the light goes.
[them,their:medieval] A hunt in the morning, a tournament after, and the hall at night.
[them,their:industrial] A fair, mostly, with races and a shooting match and too much food.
[them,their:spacer] An exhibition match, a long dinner and a great deal of talk.
[them,their:empire] With music, a fine table and everyone in their right place.
[them] Much like this, though I'd never say so to our cook.
[us] Then you'll feel at home here.
[them] Something smells good from that kitchen.
[us,us:best:Cooking] I'd tell you what it is, but I want to see your face at the table.
[us] Our cook will be glad to hear it.
[them] Then I'll save my appetite for it.
[them] At court, a feast is judged by its table and its music.
[us] We'll do our best by both.
[them] Do, and I will say so when I'm home.
[us] You brought good weather with you.
[them,their:tribal] The sky owed us a fair day for the walk.
[them] Good weather for running, and for sitting outside after.
[them] Who of yours should I bet against?
[us,trait:Kind] Nobody, we'd rather everyone went home happy.
[us] Whoever you like, they all think they'll win.
[them] Then I'll back our own and hope for the best.
[them] Your children have been watching us since we arrived.
[us] They don't see many visitors.
[them] Ours would be just the same.
[them] Where will we sleep tonight?
[us] We'll find you beds, and a floor near the warmth if we run short.
[them,their:tribal] A floor near the warmth is a bed where I come from.
[them] Either will do after a day like this.
[them] Your people play rough for a friendly day.
[us] It's a contest, not a lesson.
[them] Fair, but I'll remember it.
[them] Thank you for asking us, it's been a long time since we had a day like this.
[us] We needed one too.
[them,their:tribal] Then the spirits must have agreed to it.
[them] Then it's good for both of us.
[us] What do you make of the place, now you've seen more of it?
[them,their:industrial] Tidier than most homesteads, and your gate's well kept.
[them,their:spacer] Efficient, which I mean as a compliment.
[them] Busier than I thought, and friendlier.
[us] We'll take both.
[them] Some of ours are coming to {FEAST}, I hear.
[us] They are, and we're looking forward to it.
[them] They've talked of little else since the word came.
[us] Is there anything your people would like at {FEAST}?
[them,their:tribal] Meat, and a fair chance at your runners.
[them,their:empire] A fine table, and music if you have it.
[them,their:industrial] A race, and something to drink after.
[them] A seat at the table and a fair contest.
[us] We can manage that.
[us] Did our letter about {FEAST} reach you?
[them] It did, and I'm still thinking it over.
[us] We'd be glad to have you.
[them] I've been telling everyone at home about {FEAST}.
[us] Good things, I hope.
[them] Mostly about the food.
[us] Come again, then.
[us] It's good to see you back after {FEAST}.
[them] It was a fair day, all in all.
[us] We'll do better by you next time.
[them] At {FEAST} I sat at your table and nobody brought me a plate.
[us,trait:Kind] I'm sorry, it shouldn't have happened.
[us] We ran short, and you shouldn't have been the one to go without.
[them] I'll take that, but I haven't forgotten.
[them] {CHAMPION} still talks about the day at your colony.
[us] We still talk about losing to {CHAMPION}.
[them] It grows a little every time it's told.
[them] Our people are still sore about {CHAMPION} at {FEAST}.
[us] {CHAMPION} had a good day.
[them,their:medieval] Next tournament, we'll bring someone who can stand up to that.
[them] Next time we'll bring better.
[them] Those of ours who went to {FEAST} came back full of it.
[us] You should come next time.
[them,their:industrial] If there's a race, sign me up.
[them] Ask me, and I might.
[them] The whole town heard about {FEAST} when our people got back.
[us] What did they say?
[them,their:spacer] That your hospitality is better than your paperwork.
[them] That you feed your guests well and play fair.
[them] When is the next feast at your colony?
[us] Not before the season's out, it takes some doing.
[them] Then I'll keep my running shoes by the door.
[them] After your feast, our elders say we owe you one in return.
[us] We'd come gladly.
[them] Then bring your best runner and your strongest arm.
[them] {CHAMPION} took the day from us.
[us] Then come back and take it back.
[us] Do you remember the night after {FEAST}?
[them] I remember eating more than I should have.
[us] There'll be more next time.
[them] I'll hold you to that.
[them] I told them at court about {FEAST}.
[us] And what did the court say?
[them] That a frontier house may keep a respectable table after all.
